criteria.no: `item.text` makes that claim with nothing checkable, or makes no such claim.
criteria.unclear: Something that might be evidence is cited, but it is not clear that it supports the claim.
criteria.yes: `item.text` claims the hook was delivered with results and errors and points to at least one checkable artifact (path, commit, PR, command, test) supporting it.

evidenced.instructions: The compliance claim that matters is that the delivered work provides an optional, consumer-registered hook that runs after the bd sync and receives the sync results and errors. Does `item.text` make that claim and cite something checkable that supports it: a file path, commit, PR or diff reference, a command that was run, or a test name or test output? A bare assertion does not count. If `item.text` makes no such claim, for example it is silent, defers the hook, or describes a hook that is removed, required, closed to consumers, or not given both results and errors, answer no.

criteria.no: The account is silent about such a hook, mentions it only as a topic, plan or later work, or describes a hook that is removed, mandatory, closed to consumers, or not given both results and errors.
criteria.unclear: The account mentions a post-sync hook as delivered but it is not possible to tell whether it is given the sync results and errors.
criteria.yes: The account says the delivered work calls a hook or callback after the sync and passes it the sync results and errors, and does not make it mandatory or closed to consumers.

implemented.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires an optional post-sync hook that a consumer registers and that receives the bd sync results and errors. According to `item.text`, does the delivered work provide such a hook: something run after the sync that is given the sync's results and its errors? Count words such as post-sync hook, after-sync callback, or hook named in the row's payload. It does not count if the hook is only discussed, planned, or deferred, if it is removed, if errors or results are kept from it, if it is made mandatory, or if consumers cannot register one. Judge whether the account says this was delivered, not whether it proves it.

criteria.no: What was touched is something else: a command that only starts the existing sync, write-journal escalation, or an unrelated part of the system.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be told from the account what code or behaviour was touched.
criteria.yes: What was created, changed, or removed is the bd sync job's own behaviour, its result or failure reporting, or something that runs after a bd sync.

relevant.instructions: Identify the code or behaviour that the work in `item.text` created, changed, or removed. Is that the bd sync job's own behaviour (how it runs, what it reports, how its failures are escalated) or behaviour that runs after a bd sync? A command that merely starts the existing sync, and the write journal's own escalation, are not the sync job's behaviour. Judge only what was touched.

criteria.no: The described design does not rule it out: it provides the hook, says nothing about it, or leaves it for later.
criteria.unclear: The description touches the hook or the sync results but it cannot be told whether the design rules the required hook out.
criteria.yes: The described design explicitly rules out the required hook in one of those ways.

violated.instructions: Does the delivered design described in `item.text` rule out what `anchor.statement` requires: an optional, consumer-registered hook that runs after the bd sync and receives the results and errors? An explicit statement that no hook runs after the sync, that results and errors go only elsewhere, that errors or results are withheld from the hook, that a hook is required, or that consumers cannot register one, rules it out. Silence about the hook, or a plan to add it later, does not. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: It says the limit was not kept, only plans it, or makes no claim that it was kept.
criteria.unclear: It mentions the built-in limit but leaves the delivered cardinality uncertain.
criteria.yes: It says the delivered scheduler limits each repository to zero or one built-in sync row or refuses a second such row.

implemented.instructions: Does `item.text` state that the delivered work kept at most one built-in beads-cache bd sync schedule row for each repository? Judge the claimed delivered restriction only; silence, future intent, and discussion of scheduling alone do not state that it was kept.

criteria.no: There is no such claim, or the claim is made with nothing checkable.
criteria.unclear: Something checkable is mentioned, but it is not clear that it backs the claim.
criteria.yes: The claim is backed by at least one checkable artifact of the kinds listed.

evidenced.instructions: If `item.text` claims that bd calls, Python sync method runs, or post-sync hook runs are killed at their timeout capped by the time left before the deadline, does it cite something checkable that backs that claim: a test whose name or description concerns timeouts, deadlines, hanging processes, or kills; a source file path for that behaviour; a commit or diff; a command with its output; or a CI run? A bare claim does not count. If `item.text` makes no such claim, answer no.

criteria.no: The account does not say this: it is silent about killing at a timeout, only names the requirement or the topic, defers it, describes a process it runs as having no timeout or as exempt, or kills at a timeout not limited by the time left.
criteria.unclear: The account describes a timeout or kill, but it cannot be told whether the process is killed or whether its timeout is limited by the time left.
criteria.yes: Each process the account describes is said to be killed (terminated, stopped) at its timeout limited by the time left: wording such as min(timeout, time left), the smaller of its limit and the remaining run time, or capped by the deadline.

implemented.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that bd calls, Python sync method runs and post-sync hook runs started by beads-cache are killed at their timeout, with the timeout capped by the time left before the run's deadline. Does `item.text` say that the delivered work kills the processes it describes in this way? An account that covers only some of the three kinds counts when it says nothing about the others; what matters is that each process it describes as run is killed at a timeout limited by the time left. A requirement ID, a topic mention, or a plan for later does not count. Do not judge evidence or conflict.

criteria.no: The work does not add, change, or run any bd call, Python sync method run, or post-sync hook run: for example CI lint, release packaging, documentation, or CLI output formatting that leaves those processes unchanged.
criteria.unclear: The description is too vague to tell whether the work touches a bd call, a Python sync method run, or a post-sync hook run.
criteria.yes: The work adds, changes, or runs a bd call, a Python sync method run, or a post-sync hook run, or changes how one of them is started, timed, or stopped.

relevant.instructions: `item.text` describes delivered work. `anchor.scope` lists the kinds of work this anchor governs: work that adds or changes a bd call, a Python sync method run, or a post-sync hook run started by beads-cache. Does the delivered work in `item.text` add, change, or run one of those three kinds of process, or change how one is started, waited on, timed, or stopped? Judge only whether the work is of that kind. Do not judge whether the work complied.

criteria.no: The text states no such thing, whether or not it mentions timeouts.
criteria.unclear: The text says something about timeouts that may mean a process is unbounded or uncapped, but it is ambiguous.
criteria.yes: The text explicitly states that one of those processes has no timeout, is exempt, is awaited however long it takes, or may run past the run's deadline.

violated.instructions: Does `item.text` state that some bd call, Python sync method run, or post-sync hook run is not killed at its timeout, or is given a timeout that is not capped by the time left before the run's deadline, contrary to `anchor.statement`? Only an explicit statement of such behaviour counts. Not mentioning timeouts is not a conflict.
